page: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v5 is an entry-level general-purpose instance powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. Built upon the Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, the server delivers two dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, eliminating resource contention associated with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 8.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes an integrated 81 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch space and temporary file operations, alongside hardware AES cryptographic acceleration, while lacking discrete GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reflect the modest scale of this two-core ARM instance. Compute evaluation via stress-ng reveals mid-tier single-core throughput at 1,822.18, though multi-core processing falls into the lower quarter with 3,612.77. In cross-platform testing, Geekbench scores reach 1,107.0 in single-core and 2,008.0 in multi-core metrics, indicating limited capability for heavy parallel processing. Memory bandwidth also measures in lower performance tiers, reaching 24.09 GB/s read and 15.78 GB/s write on large uncached blocks. Application benchmarks demonstrate baseline output, yielding 2.81 GB/s in static web serving and 2.44 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency perspective, the D2pds_v5 provides a low-overhead entry point for organizations targeting the ARM64 ecosystem. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of advanced x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512, which constrains raw mathematical modeling and machine learning tasks. However, the presence of dedicated physical cores and integrated local SSD provides reliable performance for low-intensity services. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, edge container deployments, small staging environments, continuous integration test runners, and modest caching or web proxy nodes.
description: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware configurations include 81 GB of local SSD temporary storage and hardware AES cryptography support, while excluding discrete GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks place its raw computing and memory throughput in the lower tiers, reflecting its entry-level two-core capacity. Single-core stress-ng tests exhibit middle-range results, whereas multi-core compute, Geekbench ratings, and static web serving throughput indicate constrained parallel performance. Given its power-efficient ARM footprint and bundled local SSD, this server offers a cost-effective operational profile for basic tasks. The D2pds_v5 is best suited for small microservices, lightweight web backends, CI/CD runner agents, staging environments, and basic caching nodes.
